newsitem.title: USA: CNF Transportation sees lower Q4 earnings.
newsitem.headline: CNF Transportation sees lower Q4 earnings.

text.p: CNF Transportation on Thursday said earnings for its fourth quarter will be in the range of $0.35 to $0.40 a share before a charge of $0.35 a share.

Donald Moffitt, chairman, president and chief executive officer said in a statement that a higher tax rate, at about 50 percent, coupled with an increase in shares outstanding, will translate into primary earnings per share for the fourth quarter in the range of $0.35 and $0.40, or between $0.33 and $0.37 per fully diluted share before charges.
The company said year ago earnings, restated to exclude spun-off operations, were $0.42 per share, $0.39 per fully diluted share.
Analysts had predicted the company would post fourth quarter profits of $0.43 a share, according to First Call.

The transportation company said it would take a one-time $16 million charge in the fourth quarter related to its spin-off of CF MotorFreight. The $16 million charge would equal about $0.35 per primary share, $0.32 fully diluted, and includes all expenses related to the spin-off.

Moffitt also said that fourth quarter revenue and operating income from continuing operations would exceed levels in the fourth quarter of 1995. Revenues from continuing operations will be about $3.7 billion in 1996.
On December 2 the company, formerly Consolidated Freightways Inc, spun off CF MotorFreight and its related Canadian subsidiaries.
Consolidated Freightways Inc is now operating as CNF Transportation although it will not officially change its name until April when shareholders will vote on the name change.
"This charge against earnings completes the final chapter of the spin off," Moffitt said. "I'm optimistic about the new year for the CNF companies."

"Business levels in the fourth quarter have been generally good. Earnings, however, have been held back somewhat by unreimbursed higher fuel costs in October and adverse effects of work stoppages in the auto industry," Moffitt said.
